title: Extended Datacube Dimension
description: Extends the STAC Datacube Extension dimension object with two optional, additive properties for scalable dimension member dissemination: 'size' (total member cardinality) and 'definition' (a UAD-aligned URI link-out). Full dimension capabilities (provider config, parameters, hierarchy, language support, invertibility) are exposed at the OGC API - Dimensions collection endpoint referenced by 'definition'; the paginated items endpoint is discovered via the OGC API - Records rel="items" link on that collection response. A separate 'variableType' property carries the member measurement scale (UAD vocabulary).

type.description: Dimension type as defined by the STAC Datacube Extension. Coded (categorical or ranked) dimensions use 'other' and carry their measurement scale in the separate 'variableType' property below. NOTE: earlier drafts of this proposal coined 'nominal'/'ordinal' as additional 'type' values; that overlapped with existing concepts and has been withdrawn in favour of reusing the OGC API - Common Part 2 'variableType' vocabulary.

variableType.description: Measurement scale of the dimension members, reusing the OGC API - Common Part 2 'Uniform Additional Dimensions' (UAD) 'variableType' enum (schema additionalDimensionExtent.yaml). Replaces the withdrawn 'nominal'/'ordinal' 'type' values. The mapping from Stevens (1946) scales is one-to-many: a 'nominal' axis is 'numericalNominal' or 'categoricalNominal' depending on whether its member codes are numeric or categorical; likewise an ordinal axis is 'numericalOrdinal' or 'categoricalOrdinal'. NOTE: this is unrelated to stac-extensions/product, whose 'product:acquisition_type' = 'nominal' denotes a routine (non-calibration) acquisition pass, not a measurement scale; product's fields are item-level distribution metadata and do not type a dimension axis.

extent.description: The extent (minimum and maximum values) of the dimension. For hierarchical dimensions, this represents the bounds of the entire dimension across all levels. NORMATIVE: when the dimension is backed by a `provider`, the `extent` MUST be derived from the provider's generator min/max (see ExtentResult.native_min/native_max). Implementations MUST NOT permit `extent` to be configured independently of the generator. Servers SHOULD perform a startup-time assertion that the reported extent's size equals the generator's numberMatched and fail loudly on drift.

values.description: Explicit enumeration of dimension members. OPTIONAL when provider is present.

step.description: The space between dimension values. Use null for irregular spacing. Supports ISO 8601 durations for standard intervals. For non-Gregorian intervals (dekadal, pentadal), set step to null and rely on the provider to define member boundaries.

unit.description: Unit of measure. Reference UCUM or OGC Definition URIs.

reference_system.description: The spatial or temporal reference system.

size.description: Total number of discrete members in this dimension. For flat dimensions, this is the total member count. For hierarchical dimensions with leveled strategy, omit this field and use size on individual levels instead; for recursive strategy, retrieve total count from the provider. RECOMMENDED for flat and recursive dimensions.

definition.description: URI identifying the semantic concept of this dimension, reusing the OGC API - Common Part 2 UAD 'definition' property (requirement REQ_extent-uad-definition: a URI 'from any semantic definition vocabulary'). A dereferenceable OGC API - Dimensions collection endpoint URL is a conformant value: it serves as both the semantic-concept identifier and the service-discovery entry point — follow it to the collection response, then to links[rel="items"] for paginated members, plus capability links (/inverse, /children, /ancestors), hierarchy structure, language support, and conformsTo URIs. This single optional URI replaces the withdrawn 'provider' object as the entire link-out hook on the datacube side.
